recipe.notes:
One family, three sizes, the evidence for one: the pipeline files agree byte for byte (modules.json, config_sentence_transformers.json, mteb_v2_eval_prompts.json identical at all three pinned revisions; 1_Pooling/config.json differs only in word_embedding_dimension), the cards are the same text with the same usage for all three sizes, and the served path is identical: --runner pooling, convert auto -> embed, the pooler from the checkpoints' own sentence-transformers metadata (last-token + L2 normalize), causal attention, bfloat16, no plugin, no trust-remote-code, no template file. The backbones differ (Gemma3TextModel 270m/27b, Qwen3Model 0.6b) and each variant's tokenizer follows from its model id (injected per variant); the only template-visible consequence is which post-processor token the route appends (the anchor declaration covers both), and the dims 640/1024/5376 are the checkpoints' own (no Matryoshka field exists in the cards, so the client declares none). Served = the client renders the template (the query prompt for queries, bare text for documents) and POSTs strings to /v1/embeddings; vLLM v0.33.0 serves each checkpoint with --runner pooling only. Prompt format: the frame ends "Query: " WITH a trailing space -- the checkpoint's own web_search_query prompt carries it (config_sentence_transformers.json, byte-pinned) and the card's get_detailed_instruct f-string writes "Query: {query}" the same way; the other preconfigured prompts (sts_query, bitext_query) are other tasks' frames -- specialising the task means a new recipe whose frame is that prompt (a new content identity), never a per-run field. Instructions: the checkpoint's mteb_v2_eval_prompts.json holds the model's 131 per-task instructions; the task-instruction rule assigns them to Dataset.task_instruction (model-owned, per task) and this family's target placement is the card's own fold: "Instruct: <instruction>\nQuery: <text>" -- this recipe's frame is exactly that fold with the retrieval default baked in, so a task-specialised recipe replaces the Instruct text and keeps the frame (the card's own usage wins over the generic Task: prefix rule). The field's product-side plumbing ships with the embed role's title and instruction handling (the data-layer work behind those fields), so a task-specialised serving recipe is a new content identity. A per-query instruction (Query.instruction) no template slot exists for on the embed roles: the generic appended default applies product-side when a dataset carries one, and any instruction a pairs row carries is ignored on both sides of the equivalence check. Anchor: the served route appends the tokenizer's post-processor token and last-token pooling reads it -- both shapes end on their content span and pin add_special_tokens: true (the Gemma variants append the eos token, id 1, and lead with bos id 2; the 0.6b's Qwen tokenizer appends the endoftext id 151643 -- measured at the pinned revisions). The card's example (its own queries and documents) renders to 27 framed-query ids per variant and ends on the anchor (measured, pinned by the family test). Budgets: client.max_tokens is 32768 -- the card's "Max Tokens" for every variant and the transformers snippet's max_length; the cut applies to the content spans only, after reserving the frame (19-20 content ids of head, measured) and the appended anchor, and re-attaching the frame, so the anchor always survives. The card's transformers path truncates ids at 32768 (tokenizer(truncation=True, max_length=32768)); its sentence-transformers path truncates at the Transformer module's max_seq_length, which sentence-transformers infers when the checkpoint sets none (no sentence_bert_config.json, no max_seq_length in modules.json) as min(config.max_position_embeddings, tokenizer.model_max_length) (models/Transformer.py at >=3.0) -- 32768 for the 270m and the 0.6b, 131072 for the 27b -- and the post-processor appends the anchor after truncation, so it survives that cut too (measured at the pinned revisions); the client cuts verbatim text: over the cap the content boundary can differ while both keep the anchor, so the recipe declares over_cap_cut_differs, the reference's render is the card's own prompt (it never ports the client's cut), over-cap rows ride the harness's non-gating table and under-cap rows gate byte-exactly. No separate query cap exists in the referent -- the card truncates queries and documents alike at 32768 -- so query_max_tokens is not declared and both shapes draw on max_tokens. Wiring: every request is fitted to the declared budget on the wire by the merged product's embedding client (rcp.data.preprocess.fit), audited in stage 1 against the captured wire. The 27b's 131072 max_position_embeddings is NOT served: the card declares Max Tokens 32,768 for every variant (its transformers snippet truncates at 32768), and serving the full context would put the GPU-E1 32-bit element-index limits under one forward of 131072 tokens -- the MLP activation alone is 131072 x 21504 (intermediate_size) = 2.82e9 elements, over 2^31 (2,147,483,648), the fault class that killed pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview at 262144 (GPU-E1); at the card's own 32768 the same product is 32768 x 21504 = 7.0e8 elements, well under. Pooling hang: on the pre-0.32 line a pooling prompt of exactly max_model_len tokens could stick under the default chunked prefill (max_num_batched_tokens 16384 on the >=160 GB GPUs; GPU-E1). vllm-project/vllm#48039 (commit e6fc81bc78, first released in vLLM v0.32.0) fixes it in the scheduler itself (num_sampled_tokens_per_step = 0 for the pooling runner), so the backport patch this family used to declare is deleted and the family declares no patch. All three variants still reach their budget exactly: client.max_tokens == serve.max_model_len == 32768, so the client's over-cap cut lands on the documented trigger and the render declares the at-budget prompt one prefill step (the renderer declares `serve.max_num_batched_tokens` at `serve.max_model_len` when nothing sets it); no flag workaround ships (a per-variant --max-num-batched-tokens raise would re-open the 32-bit arithmetic the 27b's budget exists to avoid). The wave monitors the at-budget ladder. The engine image's transformers pin at the tag is >=5.16.1,<5.21.0 (requirements/common.txt); the tokenizer files are pinned by revision and the stage-1 zero-tolerance token-id check on the GPU host is the designed catch for library drift. No media processor settings apply: the models are text-only (input: [text], no processor files in any of the three repos). resources.gpus: 1 for every variant: the 27b's bf16 weights are ~54 GB, inside one B200. Reference environment: reference.in/reference.lock (sentence-transformers for the card's usage; render mode needs only huggingface-hub -- see reference.py).


The 27b size: a Gemma3TextModel backbone (config.json model_type gemma3_text, 62 layers in the 5:1 sliding_attention:full_attention pattern with sliding_window 1024, hidden 5376, intermediate 21504, rope_scaling linear factor 8 on the global layers, head_dim 128, 32 heads over 16 kv heads). Embedding dim 5376. max_position_embeddings is 131072 but it is NOT served: the card declares Max Tokens 32,768 for every variant, and one forward of 131072 tokens would push the MLP activation (131072 x 21504 = 2.82e9 elements) over 2^31 (the GPU-E1 32-bit element-index limits) -- see the family notes. ~54 GB of bf16 weights fit the slot's one GPU. Over-cap declaration, precisely: the card's sentence-transformers path truncates this variant at 131072 (its inferred max_seq_length), i.e. beyond the client's 32768 boundary, so at the client's cap the reference is WHOLE and the client is the only side that cuts -- the comparison over the cap is a whole-prompt vs content-cut one, not two different cut points. The only declaration that matches what the reference does is over_cap_cut_differs (anchor_drop_over_cap would be false: no anchor is dropped on either side; the post-processor appends after truncation), and its effect -- the client-changed texts are reported non-gating -- is the right one. Numerics (E2 round 4, stage 2): the served-vs-reference minimum cosine was 0.996906 over 69 vectors, with four vectors below the published 0.999 (0.996906, 0.997561, 0.997741, 0.998371) and Kendall tau 1.0. Both sides are bf16 (the engine serves the family's bfloat16 and the reference loads the checkpoint's own bfloat16, the family's one dtype rule), so the residual is the two bf16 kernel stacks -- vLLM's gemma3 kernels against the reference's sdpa -- and not a cast; this size therefore declares `overrides.gates.vec_min_cosine: 0.9969`, the tight bound covering its measured floor, with the per-vector numbers above as the evidence. The 270m and the 0.6b keep the published 0.999 (both verified). E2 re-measures.
